sections.body:
This is a story about a little rabbit named Pip. Pip is small, and Pip is brave about most things. But one thing makes Pip's ears droop: the dark.

A good story has a shape. It has a beginning, a middle, and an end. The beginning tells you who the characters are. The middle brings a problem. The end fixes the problem in a way you did not expect.

Pip's story has that shape. In the beginning, Pip cannot sleep because the burrow is dark. In the middle, Pip goes to look for the light. In the end, Pip finds that the dark was never empty at all.

The animals in this story talk like animals. They say short things. They say things that you can say too.

Listen to the story first. Then tell it back to someone. That is the best way to keep a story in your head.
examples: This story has a beginning, a middle and an end.
Pip is a little rabbit who is afraid of the dark.
I can tell this story again tomorrow.
sections.heading: What this story is about

sections.body:
Pip lives with his family under the grass. Their home has soft walls and a round door. In the morning, that door is bright. At night, it is very dark.

Pip likes many things. Pip likes cold carrots for breakfast. Pip likes jumping over the stream. Pip likes the sound of rain on the leaves.

But Pip does not like the dark. When the sun goes down, Pip's heart beats fast. Pip pulls the blanket over his head and counts to one hundred.

Counting does not help. The dark stays dark.

Then one night, Grandmother Owl knocks on the round door. She says she has something to show Pip. It is called a brave step.
examples: Pip lives in a warm home under the grass.
The dark makes Pip's heart beat fast.
Grandmother Owl has come to see Pip.
sections.heading: The beginning: Pip's big worry

sections.body:
Grandmother Owl puts a small lamp in Pip's paws. One lamp for the path, she says.

They walk into the woods. The trees grow tall. Their branches make a roof, and the lamp makes only a small circle of light. It is not very much light.

Then the wind comes. It takes the lamp out of Pip's paws. The flame goes out. Now Pip has no light at all.

Pip wants to run home. Pip's legs feel funny. Pip's tail goes small.

But Pip takes one step. Just one. Pip says the bravest word he knows: just one step.

Then Pip takes another step.
examples: The wind blew the little lamp out.
Pip is all alone, and Pip is still afraid.
One small step is enough to begin.
sections.heading: The middle: one little lamp in the woods

sections.body:
In the dark, Pip starts to notice things. There are little lights all around. They bob up and down. They are fireflies, and they glow like tiny lamps.

High above there is the moon. The sky is full of stars. Even Pip's own white tail shines a little.

The dark is not empty. It is full of small lights.

Grandmother Owl was right. The dark is only the night taking a rest, and it needs no lamp to be beautiful.

Pip walks home by the stars. Pip counts them instead of counting worries. Pip counts seven, then eight, then many more. When Pip reaches the round door, the fear is much smaller.

Well, almost smaller. There is still one dark corner. But now Pip knows that one step is enough to walk into it.
examples: The dark was full of little lights.
Pip counted the stars instead of the worries.
Pip was a little afraid, but Pip took one step anyway.
sections.heading: The surprise: the dark is full of lights

sections.body:
These are the words you will meet in this story. Learn them here, and you can use them in your own sentences.

A **burrow** is the home a rabbit digs under the ground. It is soft, it is safe, and it has a door.

A **firefly** is a very small insect that makes its own light. On a summer night you can see a whole field of them.

A **lantern** is a light you can carry. You hold it in your paw and it goes where you go.

To be **brave** is not to feel no fear at all. It is to go on anyway, one step at a time.

A **shadow** is a dark shape made when something stops the light. A big tree makes a long shadow on the path.
examples: A burrow is a rabbit's home.
The firefly glowed like a little lamp.
Brave means going on even when you are afraid.
sections.heading: The words inside Pip's story

terms.example: Pip's burrow has a round door and soft walls.
terms.gloss: The home a rabbit digs under the ground. It is soft and safe and it has a round door.

terms.example: A firefly lit the path for Pip.
terms.gloss: A very small insect that makes its own light. It glows in the dark.

terms.example: Grandmother Owl gave Pip a tiny lantern.
terms.gloss: A light you can carry in your hand. It goes wherever you go.

terms.example: Pip was brave and took one more step.
terms.gloss: Not feeling no fear, but going on anyway. Brave is about what you do, not what you feel.

terms.example: The old tree made a long shadow on the path.
terms.gloss: A dark shape that appears when something blocks the light.

sections.body:
What did Pip learn? The dark is not a monster. It is only the night taking a rest. And when you feel afraid, you do not have to be brave all at once. You can take one small step.

Here is how to tell Pip's story to someone. Keep the order. It makes the story easy to follow, and it keeps the surprise at the end.

Start with who the story is about. Tell the problem in the middle. Save the surprise for last. Then say the small lesson in one short sentence.

The lesson of Pip's story is this: one small step is enough to start.
examples: The story starts with a little rabbit named Pip.
The surprise comes at the end.
One small step is enough to start.
sections.heading: The small lesson, and how to tell the story
steps: Start by naming the character: Pip, a little rabbit.
Tell the problem: Pip cannot sleep because of the dark.
Tell the middle: the lamp goes out in the woods.
End with the surprise and the lesson: one small step.

item.summary: Pip is a little rabbit who cannot sleep because the night is dark. Follow Pip from the burrow to the woods, where a lamp goes out and something wonderful appears. After reading this story you can tell it back to someone, name the words inside it, and share the small lesson it carries.
item.title: The Little Rabbit Who Was Afraid of the Dark
